detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for [similar open PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+teacher+temperature) and [references to #7769](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+7769+in%3Abody). No matching fix was found. Related results concern distillation losses and SGLang scoring; this change applies the configured temperature to vLLM teacher logits before full-vocabulary normalization.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Design & Code Changes

- Reuse the existing `compute_logits` hook and worker startup RPC to scale teacher logits in FP32 before vLLM computes prompt logprobs, avoiding FP16 overflow and BF16 rounding during temperature division.
- Apply this scaling only to teacher replicas.
- Validate that vLLM teacher temperature is finite and positive.
- Add CPU regression tests, wire the vLLM tests into CI, and update the OPD documentation.

No vLLM source changes are required. Other teacher backends retain their existing behavior.

### API and Usage Example

With the default teacher configuration, this existing override now applies T=0.7 to both teacher scoring and student probabilities:

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.7
```

This changes teacher scores for existing configurations with a non-unit temperature. To preserve the previous teacher distribution, explicitly set:

```bash
distillation.teacher_models.teacher_model.inference.temperature=1.0
```

### Test

Focused CPU tests, using PyTorch 2.11.0 and vLLM 0.23.0:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' \
python -u -m pytest -q --durations=3 \
  tests/workers/test_distillation_temperature_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_teacher_temperature_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_vision_placeholder_tokens_on_cpu.py
```

Result: **30 passed**.

Coverage includes temperature inheritance and validation, full-vocabulary normalization, observed-token and top-k scores, token masking, and isolation from actor/reward replicas. Low-precision regression tests cover FP16 and BF16 logits at T=0.0001 and preserve the original dtype and values at T=1. Before the fix, the new low-precision cases reproduced NaN scores for FP16 and rounding errors for BF16.

```bash
uvx --with hydra-core pre-commit run --files \
  .github/workflows/vllm.yml \
  docs/algo/opd.md \
  verl/experimental/teacher_loop/teacher_manager.py \
  verl/workers/config/distillation.py \
  verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py \
  verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py \
  tests/workers/test_distillation_temperature_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_teacher_temperature_on_cpu.py
```

Result: **all 14 pre-commit hooks passed** on the changed files.

GPU end-to-end validation and runtime validation with main's pinned vLLM 0.29.0 have not been performed.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks to the changed files; commands and results are listed above.
- [x] Update the documentation (`docs/algo/opd.md`).
- [x] Add CPU regression tests and include the vLLM-specific tests in `.github/workflows/vllm.yml`.
- [x] Request CI in the `ci-request` Slack channel or Feishu group.
- [x] Recipe submodule update is not applicable.

### AI Assistance

The implementation, tests, and local validation were completed with assistance from OpenAI Codex.

@@ -663,19 +663,24 @@ rollouts on other samples.
 
 7. **Sampling params for logprob computation.** The manager builds
    sampling params with `max_tokens=1` plus `prompt_logprobs=topk` (or `0`),
-   so the teacher computes logprobs for the (prompt + response) sequence rather than
-   generating new tokens. `topk` is set to `distillation.distillation_loss.topk`
+   to score the (prompt + response) sequence. The one generated token is unused.
+   `topk` is set to `distillation.distillation_loss.topk`
    when the loss mode requires top-$k$ (e.g. `forward_kl_topk`); otherwise `0`
    (single-sample logprob only).
 
-   **Temperature is always forced to `1.0`** regardless of the configured value.
-   `prompt_logprobs` is computed via a forward pass over the existing (prompt + response)
-   tokens — no sampling occurs — so temperature has no effect on the result.
-   The default distillation config copies the student rollout temperature via Hydra
-   interpolation (`temperature: ${oc.select:actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature}`),
-   which would silently set a non-1.0 value when rollout temperature differs from 1.0
-   (e.g. 0.7). The manager ignores the configured value and always uses `temperature=1.0`,
-   logging a warning if the configured value is not 1.0.
+   **vLLM teacher scores use `inference.temperature`.** The teacher worker divides
+   logits by this temperature before vLLM computes prompt logprobs, producing
+   `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` for both sampled-token and top-$k$ scores.
+   The default configuration inherits `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature`, so
+   teacher scores and student training probabilities use the same temperature.
+   For example, setting `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.7` applies `T=0.7`
+   to both. To retain unscaled teacher scores, explicitly set
+   `distillation.teacher_models.teacher_model.inference.temperature=1.0`.
+   The teacher temperature must be finite and greater than zero.
+
+   The request's sampling temperature remains `1.0`: it does not control prompt
+   scores and only affects the unused generated token. Other teacher backends
+   retain unscaled prompt logprobs and warn when a non-1.0 temperature is configured.
 
 8. **Server-side load balancing.** The manager calls `client.generate(...)`,
    which acquires a backing server through the shared `GlobalRequestLoadBalancer`

+"""Check teacher temperature at the vLLM worker's full-vocabulary logits boundary."""
+
+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+
+pytest.importorskip("vllm")
+
+from vllm.v1.sample.sampler import Sampler
+
+from verl.workers.config import RolloutConfig
+from verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout import utils, vllm_async_server
+
+
+class FakeModel:
+    def compute_logits(self, hidden_states):
+        return hidden_states.clone()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("temperature", [0.7, 1.0, 1.5])
+def test_teacher_logprobs_match_student_temperature(temperature, monkeypatch):
+    teacher = FakeModel()
+    worker = SimpleNamespace(_iter_all_models=lambda: iter([teacher]))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(utils, "patch_vllm_moe_model_weight_loader", lambda model: None)
+    utils.vLLMColocateWorkerExtension.monkey_patch_model(
+        worker, vocab_size=4, banned_token_ids=[1], logits_temperature=temperature
+    )
+    logits = torch.tensor([[0.0, 0.8, -1.0, 2.1, 8.0], [-1.3, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0, 10.0]])
+    # vLLM's prompt path normalizes compute_logits() directly, without sampling temperature.
+    teacher_logprobs = Sampler.compute_logprobs(teacher.compute_logits(logits))
+
+    student_logits = logits[:, :4].clone()
+    student_logits[:, 1] = -torch.inf
+    student_logprobs = (student_logits / temperature).log_softmax(-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(teacher_logprobs[:, :4], student_logprobs)
+    assert torch.isneginf(teacher_logprobs[:, [1, 4]]).all()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(teacher_logprobs.exp().sum(-1), torch.ones(2))
+
+    # Both teacher top-k scores and an observed token outside top-k use full-vocabulary normalization.
+    values, ids = teacher_logprobs.topk(2, dim=-1)
+    expected_values, expected_ids = student_logprobs.topk(2, dim=-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(values, expected_values)
+    assert torch.equal(ids, expected_ids)
+    observed_ids = torch.tensor([[2], [0]])
+    assert not (ids == observed_ids).any()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(teacher_logprobs.gather(-1, observed_ids), student_logprobs.gather(-1, observed_ids))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_low_precision_teacher_scores_at_small_temperature(dtype):
+    """Temperature scaling must not overflow or round logits in the model dtype."""
+    model = FakeModel()
+    temperature = 0.0001
+    logits = torch.tensor([[20.0, 19.0, -20.0, 80.0, 100.0]], dtype=dtype)
+    utils.monkey_patch_compute_logits(model, vocab_size=4, banned_token_ids=[3], logits_temperature=temperature)
+    logprobs = Sampler.compute_logprobs(model.compute_logits(logits))
+
+    assert torch.isfinite(logprobs[:, :3]).all()
+    assert torch.isneginf(logprobs[:, 3:]).all()
+    expected = (logits[:, :3].float() / temperature).log_softmax(-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(logprobs[:, :3], expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32])
+def test_default_temperature_preserves_rollout_logits(dtype):
+    model = FakeModel()
+    logits = torch.tensor([[0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]], dtype=dtype)
+    utils.monkey_patch_compute_logits(model, vocab_size=4)
+    output = model.compute_logits(logits)
+    assert output.dtype == dtype
+    assert torch.equal(output[:, :4], logits[:, :4])
+    assert torch.isneginf(output[:, 4]).all()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", ["teacher", "actor", "reward"])
+def test_only_teacher_servers_receive_logits_temperature(role, monkeypatch):
+    replica = vllm_async_server.vLLMReplica(
+        replica_rank=0,
+        config=RolloutConfig(name="vllm", temperature=0.7, tensor_model_parallel_size=1),
+        model_config=SimpleNamespace(),
+        is_teacher_model=role == "teacher",
+        is_reward_model=role == "reward",
+    )
+    worker_info = (ray.NodeID.from_random().hex(), "0")
+    replica.workers = [SimpleNamespace(__ray_call__=SimpleNamespace(remote=AsyncMock(return_value=worker_info)))]
+    server = MagicMock()
+    server.get_master_address.remote = AsyncMock(return_value=("127.0.0.1", 1234, 1235))
+    server.get_server_address.remote = AsyncMock(return_value=("127.0.0.1", 8000))
+    server.launch_server.remote = AsyncMock()
+    replica.server_class = MagicMock()
+    replica.server_class.options.return_value.remote.return_value = server
+    monkeypatch.setattr(replica, "_get_server_name_prefix", lambda: "test_")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        vllm_async_server,
+        "get_platform",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(ray_noset_envvars=lambda: [], rollout_env_vars=lambda: {}),
+    )
+
+    asyncio.run(replica.launch_servers())
+
+    kwargs = replica.server_class.options.return_value.remote.call_args.kwargs
+    assert kwargs["logits_temperature"] == (0.7 if role == "teacher" else 1.0)

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Scale logits in float32 before normalization.**

With a float16 teacher, `temperature=0.0001` passes validation. A logit of `20` then becomes `200000` during `div_`, which exceeds float16 range. vLLM converts logits to float32 only when it later computes log-softmax, so overflow can produce NaN teacher scores and disrupt training. Convert logits to float32 before division, and cover this case in the low-precision test.
